title: Targeted versus standard peri-operative prophylaxis in patients colonized with carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales undergoing liver transplantation: a stepped-wedge cluster randomization trial
official: Targeted versus standard peri-operative prophylaxis in patients colonized with carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales undergoing liver transplantation: a stepped-wedge cluster randomization trial
summary: Main objective: To investigate the impact of T-PAP vs. S-PAP on the incidence of early CPE infection after LT in patients colonized with CPE undergoing LT
conditions: Patients colonized with CPE undergoing liver transplantation (LT)

interventions.name: Xerava 50 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
Recarbrio 500 mg/500 mg/250 mg powder for solution for infusion
Fetcroja 1 g powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
Zavicefta 2 g/0.5 g powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
Vaborem 1 g/1 g powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
Emblaveo 1.5 g/0.5 g powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
Azactam 1 g Powder for Solution for Injection or Infusion
Tygacil 50 mg powder for solution for infusion
AMOXICILLINA E ACIDO CLAVULANICO SANDOZ A/S 2000 mg/200 mg polvere per soluzione per infusione
Tazocin® 4 g / 0.5 g powder for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult (≥18 years) patients colonized with CPE undergoing liver transplantation (LT)
2. Informed consent signed by the enrolled patients
Exclusion criteria:
1. Active infection from any Gram-negative bacteria at the time of LT
2. High risk of donor-derived CPE infection (e.g., donors known to be colonized or infected with CPE at the time of death, or CPE isolated from donor blood or preservation fluid samples)
3. Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients
4. Pregnancy and breastfeeding
5. Participation in a clinical trial in which an investigational drug was administered within 30 days of screening or within the 5 half-lives of the study drug, whichever is longer.
6. History of severe immediate hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis) to beta-lactam agents (e.g., cephalosporins, carbapenems, or monobactams).
7. Colonization by strains resistant to all Investigational Medicinal Products (IMPs)
